column1: # What the odi-oss image does with each config key. Hand-written, per image,
# and the reason the UI offers 31 keys for editing instead of all 194: a key with
# no row here is not acted on by this image (omcid reads one bit of
# OMCI_CUSTOM_ME for the VEIP slot, and `omcicli` prints the other masks, which
# changes nothing). It stays in the store, and in backups and
# restores, because the config partition is shared with the stock firmware in
# the other slot, which does read it -- but it is not offered for editing.
# apply    what applying costs, shown beside the key:
#            live      takes effect at once, no interruption (a VLAN key: omcid
#                      rebuilds the connections in place, the ONU stays in O5)
#            restart   a daemon restarts; the fibre service stays up
#            internet  applied without a reboot, but the fibre service drops
#                      while it is (omcid deactivates the ONU, clears its MIB
#                      and the ONU ranges and is provisioned again)
#            reboot    only at the next boot, which also drops the service
# action   what the page runs to apply it: network (apply.sh network), omci
#          (apply.sh omci), syslog, ntp, igmp, sfp, reboot, or none (the daemon reads the key
#          each time it uses it, nothing to run). confd reports the actions a
#          save needs. omci sends SIGHUP to omcid, which rereads the store: for
#          a live key it rebuilds in place, for an internet key it re-registers
# pair     shown read-only and written together with the named key
# reader   what on the image reads it
# note     why it costs what it does
# unset    the value the image uses while the key is absent, one of its
#          options; the page shows that option selected. Required for every
#          key with an option list: the image always does something, so the
#          page never offers or shows "not set" for one.
# Source of truth for the classes: odi-oss docs/SETTINGS.md. scripts/check-schema.py
# checks every name against keys.tsv and every class and action against the lists

column6: note
/etc/config/lan-ip, when it exists, wins over this key. A change is a trial (mgmt-addr.sh): applied, kept only when confirmed over the new address.
Applied at once, with the address; a trial with it.
1 adds the second address beside the first, 0 removes it. Applied at once, as a trial; the first address is not touched.
A fixed rescue address, as br0:2. Applied at once; a trial.
Applied at once, with the second address; a trial.
An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf: empty removes it. Applied at once, as a trial with the addresses: kept only when confirmed. When only the routes change, a Keep from any client is accepted.

omcid tags only with type 1 and manual mode 1, as the stock firmware does. Applying makes omcid rebuild the bridge connections in place from the MIB it holds: the ONU stays in O5 and the fibre service is not dropped (after a failed activation it re-registers).
See VLAN config mode. Switching between stick tags and router tags (transparent) is rebuilt in place, without re-ranging the ONU.
Applying rebuilds the connections in place with the new tag; the ONU is not re-ranged.
Applied with the VLAN ID.

An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Applying rebuilds the bridge connections in place with three EAPOL rules beside the manual tag; the ONU stays in O5 (after a failed activation it re-registers). Only 1 turns it on; unset or anything else is off. Downstream one of the rules passes every priority-tagged VID 0 frame from the OLT, not only EAPOL. Without the manual tag omcid ignores the key and logs that once.

The stock firmware key and format, so both slots agree. Applying rebuilds the bridge connections in place with the new forward operation; the ONU stays in O5 (after a failed activation it re-registers). Empty: no override.
Sent to the kernel before the ONU is activated again; applying deactivates the ONU and ranges it with the new one.
Answered to CTC-profile OLTs in the LOID authentication entity. Written with LOID_OLD, because the OLD value wins whenever the two differ.
Written with LOID_PASSWD_OLD, for the same reason.
Follows LOID.
Follows LOID_PASSWD.
Reported only while the ONU identity switch is on; otherwise 0.0.0. The stock firmware may rewrite this key when it boots.
Reported only while the ONU identity switch is on; otherwise 0.0.0. The stock firmware may rewrite this key when it boots.
Reported only while the ONU identity switch is on; otherwise the device id.
Reported only while the ONU identity switch is on; otherwise 128 (0x80).
Reported only while the ONU identity switch is on; otherwise 15, the captured default.
Reported only while the ONU identity switch is on; otherwise the device id. An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf: empty removes it. Applying deactivates the ONU so the OLT reads the new version.

column5: omcid, at each software download step
column6: Read each time the OLT starts, activates or commits a software download, so a change is in effect at once and nothing is applied. An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf.

column5: omcid, at each Reboot from the OLT
column6: Read each time the OLT sends a Reboot, so a change is in effect at once and nothing is applied. An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf.
An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Changes what omcid answers the OLT for classes it does not model, so applying re-registers the ONU and the OLT provisions it again with the new answers.

column5: omcid, at start and on SIGHUP
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf: empty removes it. Applying re-registers the ONU so the OLT reads the entities again.

column5: omcid, at start and on SIGHUP
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Applying re-registers the ONU: the entities of the VEIP slot appear or disappear and the OLT provisions it again.

column5: omcid, at start and on SIGHUP, with OMCI_CUSTOM_ME bit 256
column6: The stock key, kept in the config store. Applying re-registers the ONU with the VEIP, its UNI-G, the TR-069 server, the cardholder and the circuit pack at the new entity ids, and the OLT provisions it again.

column5: omcid, at start and on SIGHUP
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Applying re-registers the ONU: the three vendor-private entities appear or disappear and the OLT provisions it again.
Needs a reboot: the MAC is set on eth0 and its host port with the links down, before br0 exists, and doing that live would cut every way in mid-change.
Applying deactivates the ONU, writes the new serial into the PON MAC (the driver accepts it only while the ONU is deactivated) and ranges it again; the OLT sees a new ONU. A reboot applies it too.
Applying restarts syslogd (init respawns it with the new address); the fibre service is not touched.
Applying restarts ntpd (init respawns it with the new server); the fibre service is not touched.
An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Applying restarts igmpd; the fibre service stays up. The switch floods for the moment the daemon is gone.
An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Applying restarts igmpd. Only 1 drops; unset or anything else does not.
An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Applying restarts igmpd. Only 1 turns MLD snooping on; unset or anything else leaves IPv6 multicast flooded. Needs IGMP_SNOOPING=1.

column5: rcs-lib.sh, the gponkeep and gponhold PON steps at boot; the driver
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Takes effect at the next boot, which drops the service. Only 0 turns it off; unset, empty or anything else keeps the disable.

column5: rcs-lib.sh, the gpondg PON step at boot; the driver reboot notifier
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Takes effect at the next boot, which drops the service.

column5: rcs-lib.sh, the laser PON step at boot
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Takes effect at the next boot, which drops the service.

column5: omcid, at every ME 11 Set, MIB reset and start
column6: Read each time the OLT sets the port state, so a change is in effect at once and nothing is applied. An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. A MIB reset or a restart always unlocks the port, and a safe-mode boot turns the setting off.

column5: omcid, at every Get and MIB upload
column6: Read at every Get and MIB upload, so a change needs no reload and no re-registration. An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf.

column5: omcid, at start and on SIGHUP (re-registers)
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Applying re-registers the ONU: the phone entities appear or disappear and the OLT provisions it again.

column5: omcid, at every Get of the VoIP line status
column6: Read at every Get of the line status, so a change needs no reload and no re-registration. An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf.

column5: sfp-host-ddm.sh: a PON step at boot, and apply.sh sfp; the kernel does the rest (odi_switch.sfp_mirror)
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Takes effect at once with apply.sh sfp, no reboot and the fibre service is not touched. 1, empty or absent serve it; any other value serves it and logs a bad value.
